experiment: NTFS-3G/FUSE versus read-only kernel NTFS3 on the same Samsung 870 EVO model SSD

device.storage: Samsung SSD 870 EVO 1TB through Innostor IS621 USB 3 bridge
device.usb_interface: Mass Storage SCSI Bulk-Only protocol 80; no UAS interface

a41_binary_compatibility.reason: NTFS-3G-created POSIX symlinks in build/bin were not represented as usable ELF symlinks by kernel NTFS3; the dynamic loader reported libllama-common.so.0 file too short. Copying the 11 MiB runtime bundle to the native Linux SD filesystem fixed startup without copying the model.

a42_end_to_end_screen.model_storage: same single 48 GB SSD model file
a42_end_to_end_screen.swap: disabled during run and restored afterwards with zero used bytes
a42_end_to_end_screen.screening_note: The run was intentionally stopped during decode after the prefill regression. A concurrent read-only source grep may have added some SSD contention, so wall time is not promoted as a precise comparison; the 65.70 percent prefill loss is large enough to reject this mmap path without another long run.

reason: Kernel NTFS3 improved controlled 1 MiB direct random reads but severely regressed the real mmap page-fault workload. Keep NTFS-3G/FUSE for the current model and move the next experiment to application-level coalesced or direct I/O rather than changing the default filesystem.
